nodes.label: Cognitive Map layer, Phase 1 (complex numbers)
nodes.rationale: The app knew HOW MANY answers were right at sub-topic resolution but not WHAT broke. This layer maps every answer to a named skill and a named misconception, runs local knowledge tracing, and emits one recommendation plus one Hebrew insight sentence — with zero new storage, zero API calls, and zero changes to verified content. Scope deliberately limited to math5 / מספרים מרוכבים, 5 sub-topics.

nodes.label: Super-principle: don't move state — derive it
nodes.rationale: All cognitive state is a pure function of the existing event log + a static catalog + the clock. This means no migration, no sixth store, no drift (state can never desync from evidence), full replay for synthetic students, free updates after every answer, and it is cheap: ≤1000 events × ~18 skills in one useMemo (<2ms). A separate bagrut-evidence-v1 store was explicitly rejected because it adds a second write path and a second sync target that can diverge.

nodes.label: buildCognitiveState(events, catalog, now) — the single public entry point
nodes.rationale: Every module under lib/cognition/ is a pure function with no React, no localStorage and no internal Date.now() — the clock is always a `now` parameter. That is exactly what makes the layer fully testable and deterministic.

nodes.label: ResultEvent extension: kind, chosenIndex, hintUsed, optionCount
nodes.rationale: The single exception to 'derive, don't store': ResultEvent did not record WHICH distractor was chosen, so 'met the misconception and did not fall for it' was indistinguishable from 'never met it'. Four optional fields on an already-written event carry zero behavioral risk, unlike a separate evidence store. chosenIndex is the ORIGINAL index, not the shuffled one.

nodes.label: TopicCognitionMap catalog (content/cognition/)
nodes.rationale: The catalog lives in a separate file keyed by questionId rather than inside content/lessons/math5/complex-numbers.ts (4,160 lines, mathematically verified, concurrently modified). Result: zero risk to verified content, zero conflict with parallel sessions, and adding a topic is one file plus one registry line.

nodes.label: Skill type (id, prereqs, band)
nodes.rationale: SkillIds are namespaced strings ('cx.arg.quadrant') meant to be stable forever. `band` (easy/mid/hard) sets the BKT prior; `prereqs` is what makes the weakest-link diagnosis possible at all.

nodes.label: Misconception type (triggers, rootSkill, remedy, insight)
nodes.rationale: A misconception carries the skill it corrupts, an optional upstream rootSkill, the single Hebrew sentence shown on screen, a remedy pointing at an existing ladder destination, and `triggers` — (questionId, optionIndex) pairs where choosing that option IS the misconception. Open questions get optional `probes` checked through checkAnswer.

nodes.label: Complex-numbers skill prerequisite graph (18 planned / 22 built)
nodes.rationale: Resolution chosen at 18 skills (3-4 per sub-topic) rather than 8 (too coarse) or 30 (many skills would never accumulate evidence). Shipped at 22, each covered by at least one question, enforced by the gate.

nodes.label: BKT-lite knowledge tracing
nodes.rationale: Chosen over weighted accuracy because it (a) produces a probability so 'certainty' is a natural concept, (b) models guessing explicitly — critical when most questions are 4-option MCQ at 25% guess rate, (c) is a ~15-line incremental update. slip=0.10, transit=0.15, guess=1/optionCount for MCQ, 0.05 for machine-checked open, 0.15 for self-reported. hintUsed && correct skips the Bayes step and applies half transit, because correct-with-a-hint is not evidence of independent mastery; isReplay bumps guess to 0.5 since repeating a familiar question is weak evidence.

nodes.label: Forgetting decay (21-day half-life, applied at read time)
nodes.rationale: p_now = p0 + (p_last − p0)·2^(−Δdays/21). Applied on read rather than persisted, consistent with the derive-don't-store principle; the same 21-day recency weight w(t) is reused for misconception rates.

nodes.label: Misconception detection by lookup, not guessing
nodes.rationale: A chosen distractor index is looked up in the trigger table — no AI, no heuristics, no false positives, because a human already wrote in Hebrew what each distractor means; the layer only gives it an id. Answering a triggered question correctly counts as an 'opportunity' ('met it and didn't fall for it'). rate uses Laplace smoothing plus recency weighting; status walks resolved → fading → suspected → active.

nodes.label: Diagnose the weakest link in the prerequisite graph
nodes.rationale: Candidates are skills with evidence in the last 14 days in state fragile/developing; for each transitive prereq (depth ≤2) that is fragile, has confidence ≥0.35 and a gap p(child)−p(prereq) ≥0.15, a break is proposed. Largest gap wins, ties broken by graph depth then catalog order. This is what produces the target sentence: 'your problem isn't the complex roots — it's the quadrant fix in the argument before them.'

nodes.label: Next-best-step single arbitrator
nodes.rationale: Before this there were three separate voices — getResumePoint, dueItems, weakestSubTopics — and nothing adjudicated between them. Priorities: prereq-repair 100 × severity, misconception-drill 80 × weight, review-due 60, continue-ladder 40, consolidate 20, start 5; score = priority × urgency with deterministic tie-breaks. Critically the arbitrator never invents destinations — every href points at a screen that already exists.

nodes.label: Insight sentences from templates, not AI
nodes.rationale: Five Hebrew templates (prereq-break, misconception, fragile-recent, decayed, too-little). The last returns null on purpose: a diagnosis is not invented from 2 questions. Templates keep the whole feature at $0 Anthropic cost.

nodes.label: Separating "he is weak" from "we don't know"
nodes.rationale: SkillMastery carries `confidence` separately from `p`: confidence = 1 − exp(−effectiveN/3). Below the threshold the state is `unknown`, never `fragile`. This is the mechanism that prevents false accusations built on no evidence.

nodes.label: MIN_CONFIDENCE raised to 0.5 (deviation from plan)
nodes.rationale: Testing showed 0.35 classified a student as `fragile` after just TWO answers. 0.5 sits between 2 and 3 observations. Biasing toward leniency is the expensive mistake — it turns 'we didn't measure' into 'you are weak at this'.

nodes.label: Merging prereq-repair with misconception-drill (deviation from plan)
nodes.rationale: When the strongest misconception sits ON the broken prereq they are the same conclusion at two resolutions. The first run had the headline blaming the argument while the button offered something else — a diagnosis and a prescription that contradict each other read as a bug even when both are correct. Now one candidate is emitted, phrased from the (more precise) misconception but carrying the prereq's priority. An invariant test locks this.

nodes.label: hePrefix — Hebrew definite-article prefixing
nodes.rationale: Naive concatenation 'ב' + 'ההצגה' yields 'בההצגה'. Most skill titles are definite, so nearly every generated sentence would have been ungrammatical. A title opening with math gets a dash instead, matching the content style.

nodes.label: scripts/verify-cognition.ts — catalog integrity gate
nodes.rationale: Enforces: no orphan SkillId, no missing prereq, NO CYCLES in the graph, every trigger points at a real MCQ question and an in-range optionIndex that is NOT the correct answer (catching the 'marking a right answer as an error' class), no two misconceptions claiming the same distractor, every remedy resolving to an existing ladder rung, ≥10 misconceptions, every skill covered by a question. It explicitly cannot judge whether a misconception is the right reading of a distractor — that came from hand-reading all 186 distractor notes. Ships 0 errors, 14 warnings; the 14 are misconceptions whose triggers all sit on one question, which is an inventory limit and the next authoring worklist, not a bug.

nodes.label: scripts/test-cognition.ts — algorithm tests (fixed clock)
nodes.rationale: Written in the verify-review.ts house style (localStorage shim, fixed clock, PASS/FAIL). Covers BKT monotonicity, guess weighting (a single correct MCQ lifts p less than a correct open question), hint discounting, 42-day decay returning p halfway to prior, 2 observations → unknown not fragile, misconception rate 2/2 vs 2/9, and arbitrator determinism. 61/61 at phase 3, 68/68 after bagrut-part mapping.

nodes.label: Synthetic-student replay as the real proof
nodes.rationale: Three archetypes are replayed through the same pure function and asserted on the exact Hebrew sentence produced: the quadrant-confuser, the forgot-the-nth-root student, and the steady student — for whom the required output is insight = null and nextStep = continue-ladder, i.e. NOT inventing a problem.

nodes.label: CognitiveInsightCard (phase 4 UI on /roadmap)
nodes.rationale: One component plus 3 wiring lines in app/roadmap/page.tsx, shown above the daily-review card. No new screen and no new navigation item. Live-verified on the public /roadmap (checkable without login): full card for the quadrant-confuser, no DOM node at all for the steady student, insight-without-CTA for legacy events lacking chosenIndex, correct bidi, no 375px horizontal overflow, 0 console errors, working deep-link.

nodes.label: Silence is a valid render (return null)
nodes.rationale: With no insight and no active misconception the component returns null. A panel that always has something profound to say about a student who answered 4 questions is a horoscope, and students recognize it.

nodes.label: No competing CTA on /roadmap
nodes.rationale: /roadmap already has two buttons (daily review, resume), and next-step.ts may legitimately pick them; in that case the card shows only the REASON and draws no button. It renders a button only for prereq-repair and misconception-drill — the two kinds no other card offers. After seeing it in the browser, two headings both read 'הצעד הבא שלך', so the button became 'לתקן קודם — לפני שממשיכים', turning a collision into a sequence; the heading also now names the topic, since the page lists 10 topics.

nodes.label: Bagrut parts mapped to skills under `${questionId}-${partLabel}`
nodes.rationale: QuestionPartCard logs one event PER PART under a composite id like cx-bag-001-א — the bare question id never reaches results.ts, so any mapping keyed on cx-bag-001 would point at nothing. Explicit per-part mapping (26/26 by hand) is required because a bagrut question deliberately crosses skills (part א converts to polar, ב powers, ג returns to algebraic); a sub-topic fallback would both destroy that information and let a 5-part question emit ~35 observations and flood the tracer. A test locks it: 3 parts produce 6 observations, not 21.

nodes.label: ResultEvent.selfReported — who graded the answer
nodes.rationale: false = lib/answer-check compared symbolically (or the AI judge); true = the student saw the solution and marked himself. guessFor prices them differently: 0.05 machine-graded, 0.25 self-reported (the generous grader in the app), 0.15 unknown (events written before the field existed). Without it a session of generous self-reporting would read as mastery. Applied to QuestionRunnerCard's two paths as well.

nodes.label: Results-log sync to Supabase by set union, not max-wins
nodes.rationale: learning_state.results already existed in supabase-learning-path.sql ('reserved for later phases'), so zero migration is needed. The roadmap store is a monotonically-advancing map where max-wins converges; the answer log is an append-only sequence, so the correct merge is set union keyed on (ts, source, questionId, subject, topic). The merge preserves unknown fields structurally — rebuilding field-by-field would have erased chosenIndex/selfReported/optionCount and blinded lib/cognition for every syncing student. test-sync.ts is 28/28, and its central test is that merge(a,b) equals merge(b,a), because order-dependent merging gives two devices two different grade predictions.

nodes.label: `repeat` is re-derived on merge, never merged
nodes.rationale: `repeat` means 'this was already answered before', but each device only knew its own history, so both rightly recorded 'first attempt' for the same question; a naive union would count both as measurements and inflate the predicted grade. Recomputing over the merged, sorted log is order-independent AND repairs flags that were wrong while devices were disconnected. The derived 'already counted' set is therefore not synced — it is rebuilt locally.

nodes.label: 200KB payload guards (byte-identical skip + 15s debounce)
nodes.rationale: A full log is ~200KB of JSON against ~10KB for the map, and students are on phones. Two guards: skip the write entirely when the merged body is byte-identical to the previous one (visibilitychange and beforeunload fire right after a push and would otherwise re-upload the same 200KB), and debounce 4s → 15s while keeping an immediate flush on page exit. Defensively, the SELECT is `*` rather than a column list and a failed upsert retries without `results`, so a missing column on an old-schema table cannot take down the already-working map sync. recordResult now marks dirty, otherwise an answer only reached the server on the next unrelated write.

nodes.label: distractorNotes — 65 pre-written misconceptions being thrown away
nodes.rationale: complex-numbers.ts already had 65 MCQ questions all carrying distractorNotes — every distractor is an articulated, verified Hebrew misconception. When a student clicked distractor #2 the system displayed the note and logged category 'אחר', losing the misconception's identity. The signal was already in the click; only the display used it. Also relies on seededOrder(n, q.id) shuffling being deterministic while `selected` stays the ORIGINAL index, making chosenIndex a clean signal. Shipped: 46 misconceptions, 186 triggers, 103 mapped questions.

nodes.label: ErrorCategory collapses to 'אחר' — why misconceptionId stays separate
nodes.rationale: ErrorCategory defaults to 'אחר' with manual re-tagging, and an incident is already documented where /errors announced '100% of your mistakes are of type other'. ErrorCategory is a taxonomy FOR THE USER; misconceptionId is a DIAGNOSTIC identifier. Merging them would reproduce exactly that collapse. A one-way misconceptionId → ErrorCategory mapping for display is fine later; a union is not.

nodes.label: Five disconnected localStorage stores (audit)
nodes.rationale: results / roadmap-progress / mistakes / review / study-plan each keep their own key, and roadmap-sync only pushes roadmap and plan to Supabase — so results, mistakes and review (the diagnostic substrate) existed only on the current device. This audit is the reason the plan added results to sync later.
